verdict.rationale: OpenClaw docs describe a dedicated secrets subsystem — additive SecretRefs so credentials don't need to live as plaintext in config, plus a shared secret store, runtime snapshots, and 'safe one-way scrubbing' (openclaw-docs-14, openclaw-docs-95) — which aligns with the deliberate credential-handling story. A security audit command also flags configuration drift (openclaw-docs-12/47). However, this is vendor documentation only, with no independent/hands-on confirmation, and no explicit claim that secrets are redacted from chat transcripts or agent context specifically (as opposed to config files); community commentary instead focuses on broad tool-execution risk (openclaw-comm-4) rather than credential redaction. Missing for 10: independent/hands-on verification of the SecretRef and scrubbing mechanism, explicit documentation that secrets are redacted from chat/session logs (not just config), and confirmation that all supported integrations require SecretRefs rather than optional plaintext.
